questions.prompt: How does the quiz engine divide responsibilities between its classes? Explain what App does and deliberately does not do, what QuestionLoader keeps apart and what kind of class it is, what QuizEngine knows and does not know, what QuizResult works from, and why QuestionAttempt exists.

keyPoints.text: App is the coordinator: it tells the right class to do the right job instead of doing everything itself.
keyPoints.quote: It does not do everything itself. Instead, it tells the right class to do the right job.

keyPoints.text: App does not parse the question file and contains no scoring rules.
keyPoints.quote: It does not parse the question file itself and it does not contain the scoring rules.

keyPoints.text: QuestionLoader keeps file I/O and parsing separate from the gameplay.
keyPoints.quote: This keeps file I/O and parsing separate from the quiz gameplay.

keyPoints.text: QuestionLoader is a repository-style class: the class that gets questions from storage.
keyPoints.quote: the class that gets questions from storage.

keyPoints.text: QuizEngine knows how to ask questions and collect answers but not how to read the file.
keyPoints.quote: It knows how to ask questions and collect answers, but it does not know how to read the file.

keyPoints.text: QuizResult asks nothing; it only works with the completed list of attempts and computes totals.
keyPoints.quote: It only works with the completed list of attempts and computes the totals.

keyPoints.text: QuestionAttempt keeps quiz history in a clean structure instead of many separate variables.
keyPoints.quote: it keeps quiz history in a clean structure instead of spreading it across many variables.

questions.prompt: Why does the quiz engine store questions in a custom one-line text format rather than JSON? Give the format's advantages the README lists, the reason JSON is a poor fit in plain Java, and the deciding goal behind the choice.

keyPoints.text: The project uses a simple custom text format instead of JSON.
keyPoints.quote: The project uses a simple custom text format instead of JSON.

keyPoints.text: It is easy to read and easy to edit by hand.
keyPoints.quote: it is easy to edit by hand

keyPoints.text: It avoids needing a JSON library.
keyPoints.quote: it avoids needing a JSON library

keyPoints.text: The parser stays short enough for a beginner to understand.
keyPoints.quote: the parser stays short enough for a beginner to understand

keyPoints.text: Plain Java has no beginner-friendly built-in JSON parser.
keyPoints.quote: Plain Java does not include a built-in JSON parser that is beginner-friendly.

keyPoints.text: Parsing JSON without a library would be more complicated than the quiz itself.
keyPoints.quote: the parsing code would become more complicated than the quiz itself.

keyPoints.text: Because the goal is learning core Java, a simple text format fits better.
keyPoints.quote: Since the goal is learning core Java, a simple text format is a better fit.

questions.prompt: Why is the quiz engine split into exactly these classes, neither one file nor many layers? State the two goals the structure balances, what would go wrong in a single file, the risk on the other side, what the chosen design teaches, and the recommended study order with its reasoning.

keyPoints.text: The structure balances being small enough for a beginner with being organized enough to teach good habits.
keyPoints.quote: organized enough to teach good habits

keyPoints.text: In one file, file reading, question data, the menu, the quiz loop and scoring would all mix together.
keyPoints.quote: file reading, question data, the menu, the quiz loop, and scoring would all mix together.

keyPoints.text: That would be harder to read and harder to change.
keyPoints.quote: That becomes harder to read and harder to change.

keyPoints.text: Going the other way risks too many layers and abstractions for a beginner.
keyPoints.quote: adding too many layers and abstractions

keyPoints.text: The design teaches separation of concerns without making it feel magical.
keyPoints.quote: This teaches separation of concerns without making the design feel magical.

keyPoints.text: Study the data objects first (Question, QuestionAttempt, QuizResult).
keyPoints.quote: first learn the data objects

keyPoints.text: Then how data is loaded, then how the quiz runs, and finally how App coordinates everything.
keyPoints.quote: finally learn how the whole app is coordinated
